strategy.summary: Reproduce NumPy indexing correctness regression: for a specific flat index (8193) when using 1-D indices with shape (8194,) and reusing them to generate 2-D coordinates via np.unravel_index (with output shape (8194, 1) on inputs shaped (8194,1)), the round-trip via np.ravel_multi_index miscomputes the column coordinate by -1 on exactly one element at the boundary. The reproduction uses the project’s provided regression test target in numpy/lib/tests/test_index_tricks.py.

pinned_because: Use NumPy 2.3.4 because the documented era constraint in the provided evidence explicitly references 2.3.4 and the bug report is tied to the indexing round-trip behavior across versions; other versions are mentioned but 2.3.4 is the documented minimum for this reproduction.
pytest and hypothesis are required by NumPy’s own README testing guidance; no additional constraints are provided by the evidence.

strategy.reproducing_test:
In numpy/lib/tests/test_index_tricks.py, run TestRegression.test_unravel_index_buffer_boundary (as added by the provided diff):

indices = np.arange(10_000, dtype=np.intp)[:, None]
coords = np.unravel_index(indices, (100, 100))
assert_array_equal(np.ravel_multi_index(coords, (100, 100)), indices)

This is designed to hit the reported boundary mismatch (first at flat index 8193) with intp/shape (10000,1).
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy NumPy revision (BUGGY COMMIT 279da819df8c), the test assertion fails because the round-trip produces at least one mismatched element (specifically the coordinate/value corresponding to flat index 8193), causing pytest’s array-equality assertion to raise an AssertionError. On the fixed revision, the same assertion passes with full equality.
strategy.numerical_probe: Not independently checked. The only oracle is the full array equality in the regression test; that equality will be violated at flat index 8193 on the buggy revision and will hold for all indices on the fixed revision.

input_output_examples.input: flat index 8193 (constructed by indices = np.arange(10_000, dtype=np.intp)[:, None] feeding into coords = np.unravel_index(indices, (100, 100)); then round-tripped via np.ravel_multi_index(coords, (100, 100))) with observed 2-D coordinate miscomputed under the reported setup
input_output_examples.buggy_output: 2-D returned coordinate (for the mismatching element) is (8, 192) instead of (8, 193); therefore the round-tripped value at that position is 8192 instead of 8193
input_output_examples.expected_output: 2-D returned coordinate should be (8, 193), and the round-tripped value at that position should be 8193

input_output_examples.input: flat index 8192 under the same setup (first non-failing neighbor noted in evidence)

risks: The evidence does not provide the exact location of the bug in terms of which underlying API is responsible beyond the regression test using np.unravel_index and np.ravel_multi_index; however, the provided diff indicates the authoritative test to run. Stick to the test as written to ensure you hit the same internal path.

The manifestation is sparse (1 mismatch out of 8194; first mismatch at flat index 8193). If the reproduction deviates from the test’s exact array shapes/dtypes ((10000,1) indices, dtype np.intp, target shape (100,100)), the specific boundary element may not be the first or may not mismatch.

Platform/toolchain dependence is possible (the evidence specifies GCC 8.5.0 on Red Hat); if the bug is sensitive to architecture or compiler optimizations, the failure may not reproduce on other toolchains. If you cannot match the platform, expect a risk that the test may pass even on a buggy revision.

The evidence specifies a buggy commit hash but does not include a method to install/checkout that exact commit; you must ensure your environment actually runs NumPy built from 279da819df8c for the failing case and the corresponding fixed commit for the passing case.

oracle.why: The regression test uses assert_array_equal on the entire integer array produced by np.ravel_multi_index(coords, (100,100)) and compares it exactly to the original indices array.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: pytest will fail on the buggy NumPy revision with an AssertionError from assert_array_equal, because the round-trip equality breaks at least at the element corresponding to flat index 8193 (observed as expected (8,193) vs returned (8,192), producing round-tripped value 8192 instead of 8193).
strategy.passes_on_fixed: pytest will pass on the fixed NumPy revision because np.unravel_index and subsequent np.ravel_multi_index round-trip correctly for all indices generated by np.arange(10_000, dtype=np.intp)[:, None] into the (100,100) grid.
